problem: Existing VLN training feeds R2R samples uniformly and ignores their difficulty distribution; agents even fail on easy in-room navigation samples on seen environments (about 50% of first errors are wrong in-room direction).
motivation: Prior work improves models, augmentation or pre-training, but rarely asks how well the agent exploits the existing data. Easy single-room tasks are handled poorly, so a curriculum from easy to hard could improve performance, generalization and training efficiency without changing the model or data.
key_idea: Re-split R2R into 5 rounds by the number of rooms the path passes through (CLR2R) and train the agent with an adapted self-paced curriculum learning (SPCL) that combines this human prior with loss-based sample weights.
insight: The gain comes from the easy-to-hard ordering rather than from sample ordering itself: random order and reversed-order curricula give no gain or hurt (e.g. Follower val-unseen SR 28.1 random, 28.9 reverse vs 32.2 SPCL). The loss-range plots suggest curriculum smooths the loss landscape, and SPCL is more consistently beneficial than naive CL, which hurts Follower on seen splits and EnvDrop on unseen.
method: CLR2R curriculum design: difficulty is room length R(p), the number of rooms on the GT path; the R2R train set is split into 5 disjoint rounds (1,2,3,4 rooms, and 5+ rooms), val/test unchanged
Naive CL (NCL): train on round 1, then rounds 1-2, and so on up to the full CLR2R train set
SPCL objective: minimizes the sum of w_i*loss_i + g(w;λ) with w constrained to a curriculum region Φ={a^T w ≤ c}, where a_i=i for round-i samples and c is in [0.95‖a‖1, ‖a‖1]
Self-paced functions: binary (w=1[ℓ≤λ]) and linear (w=1[ℓ≤λ](1-ℓ/λ)); w is solved by projected gradient descent in the region
Modified ACS algorithm: replaces the exact θ minimization with T SGD steps, then updates w and increases λ by step μ (λ is increased by μ if it is below the maximum item loss, otherwise by μ/2)
Model-agnostic application to Speaker-Follower, Self-Monitoring and EnvDrop; for EnvDrop only the imitation (GT trajectory) loss drives weight updates
Initialization: rounds 1-2 start with weight 1 and rounds 3-5 with w0; λ starts at 2

setting.backbone: Speaker-Follower, Self-Monitoring and EnvDrop agents (trained from scratch, reproduced in a unified codebase)
setting.training_data: R2R train set only (rearranged as CLR2R), with no data augmentation; extra experiments use RxR-en and FGR2R
setting.observation: panoramic RGB views in the Matterport3D simulator, with instruction text
setting.privileged: none (room counts of training paths are used only to build the curriculum)

numbers_note: Seen-split and other-model numbers are in Table 1; only the SPCL rows are listed for val-unseen and test. Naive CL sometimes beats SPCL on val-seen (Self-Monitoring) and test SR (Self-Monitoring: 40.8).
results: SPCL improves all three agents on R2R val-unseen SR: Follower 28.6→32.2, Self-Monitoring 38.4→41.0, EnvDrop 45.7→47.6, and SPL improves consistently, with faster learning. On test, EnvDrop reaches 48.4 SR/45.5 SPL vs 46.5/43.5, but Self-Monitoring SR drops slightly (39.3 vs 40.5).
limitations: Gains are modest and sometimes not consistent (naive CL hurts Follower on val-seen; SPCL does not improve Self-Monitoring on test); seed variance is comparable to some gains
The difficulty definition (room count) is hand-designed and specific to R2R; the modified algorithm lacks a convergence guarantee
Tested only with older LSTM-based agents on R2R, without back-translation augmentation, and below the state of the art
